top_stories.title: Who was Kamran Aman? UK delivery driver stabbed to death in racist attack by teenagers - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Marcus Staniforth**, 17, and a 16-year-old boy were sentenced to life in prison with minimum terms of 17 years and 15 years respectively for the racist murder of **Kamran Aman**, a 38-year-old grocery delivery driver. The attack occurred outside **Aman's** mother's home in Barry, Wales, after the victim was targeted by the teenagers who had been drinking alcohol and taking drugs.  The case has now been referred to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme for review.

top_stories.title: Quad remains ‘vital’, says Japanese Foreign Minister, rejecting concerns over the grouping’s importance in the Indo-Pacific - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Toshimitsu Motegi**, **Japanese Foreign Minister**, stated that the **Quadrilateral Foreign Ministers' Meeting (FMM)** will prioritize cooperation on critical minerals for green energy and hi-tech. The meeting, hosted by **S. Jaishankar**, will also address ongoing conflicts in Iran and the Hormuz Strait blockade, as well as the recent visit of **Donald Trump** to China.  The FMM is expected to set the agenda for the Quad Summit, which has not taken place since 2024 due to India-U.S. tensions.

top_stories.title: What we know about the possible US-Iran deal - World - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** announced an agreement had been “largely negotiated” with **Iran**, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.  **Esmaeil Baqaei**, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, stated that a memorandum of understanding (MoU) would be drafted first, before a final deal is reached within 30 to 60 days. The agreement reportedly includes an apparent commitment by **Iran** to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, but **Iran** has denied making any commitments regarding its nuclear program.  A key sticking point in the talks is traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global conduit for oil shipments that has come under Iranian control since the outbreak of the war. The potential agreement would also see the US temporarily lifting sanctions on oil, gas, and petrochemicals during the negotiation period.

top_stories.title: Blast hits train in Pakistan’s Balochistan, killing at least 24 people | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: A bomb attack on a train carrying military personnel in Quetta, Balochistan, Pakistan, killed at least 24 people and injured over 50. The explosion occurred near the Chaman Pattak signal as the train passed, causing two carriages to overturn and catch fire. **The Balochistan Liberation Army** claimed responsibility for the attack.

top_stories.title: Andy Burnham seeks advice from Sue Gray on forming future Labour government | Andy Burnham | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Andy Burnham** has sought advice from **Sue Gray**, former chief of staff to **Keir Starmer**, on managing a potential transition into Downing Street.  Senior Labour figures are increasingly treating Burnham's path back to Westminster seriously, with internal succession chatter intensifying ahead of the Makerfield byelection.  **Darren Jones**, chief secretary to the Treasury, criticized the internal jockeying and urged focus on addressing country-wide challenges. **Wes Streeting**, a potential rival contender in any future leadership race, campaigned for Burnham over the weekend alongside **Lucy Powell**, Labour's deputy leader.

top_stories.title: Indian man Parminderpal Singh arrested by ICE in Los Angeles over criminal record, may face deportation - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)** arrested **Parminderpal Singh**, a 26-year-old Indian citizen, in Los Angeles this week for potential deportation proceedings.  Singh has a history of criminal offenses including vehicle theft, grand theft, trespassing, and vandalism. This arrest follows a trend of ICE targeting non-citizens accused or convicted of crimes, with several Indian nationals facing detention or deportation proceedings in recent years.

top_stories.title: New U.S. Green Card rules raise concerns among professionals, students - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Trump administration's** new immigration policy requiring non-immigrant visa holders to apply for permanent residency in their home countries has caused anxiety and uncertainty among Indian professionals and students living in the United States. The policy, implemented through a memo from **USCIS**, requires most temporary workers and students to leave the country and apply for permanent residency through consular processing, creating concern for those already facing lengthy Green Card backlogs.  Many individuals, including software engineers like Maddela Srinivasulu and parents like Bulusu Janardhan, express fear about the future of their families and careers in the U.S., while others believe the policy's impact will be limited due to existing wait times for employment-based Green Cards.

top_stories.title: PM Shehbaz lands in Beijing, will hold 'high-level' meetings with Chinese leadership - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif** arrived in Beijing on Sunday to meet with Chinese leadership, including President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang.  He discussed strengthening the Pakistan-China all-weather strategic cooperative partnership and advancing cooperation under CPEC Phase-II. **Shehbaz** highlighted areas of importance for Pakistani-Chinese cooperation, such as agriculture, IT, special economic zones (SEZs), and mining. He also emphasized the potential of renewable energy, healthcare, and investment opportunities in Pakistan.  **DPM Ishaq Dar**, accompanied by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, arrived in Beijing to participate in the 2nd Pakistan–China Political Parties Forum and the 4th CPEC Political Parties Joint Consultation Mechanism. **Dar** highlighted Pakistan's economic revival and emphasized a billion-dollar joint venture between Servis Group of Pakistan and Long March Tyres of China.  The visit is significant as Pakistan and China commemorate the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations.

top_stories.title: Will the Texas primary run-off give Democrats a chance to flip the state? | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: The Texas Republican primary runoff between Attorney General Ken Paxton and Senator John Cornyn will determine the nominee for November's midterm elections.  Paxton, endorsed by former President Donald Trump, faces accusations of misconduct and is considered less likely to win against Democratic nominee James Talarico, who has gained momentum in recent polls. Republicans are concerned that a Paxton nomination could hurt their statewide prospects and potentially lead to a shift in power within the US Senate. The winner will face Talarico, a left-leaning candidate with strong support from independent voters.

top_stories.title: Trump turnaround: Open the straits, close the war - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** has reportedly shifted his approach to the ongoing conflict with **Iran**, aiming for a deal that falls short of initial demands. The agreement, which would involve concessions from the U.S., aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and prevent global economic disruptions caused by energy supply issues.  However, Iran insists on maintaining sovereignty over the waterway and has rejected commitments regarding uranium enrichment or nuclear program dismantlement.
